passage: Notice of license suspension, Board of Elevator Safety, in the matter of Corvus Lift Services, license 3319. Following the inspection of March 3 at the Delmar Arcade, the Board finds that respondent returned elevator 2 to service without completing the governor test required after replacement of the governor rope, contrary to rule 8.11. The elevator operated for six days before the omission was discovered during a routine audit of test certificates; no incident occurred during that period, and a governor test performed under Board observation on March 12 was passed. The Board nonetheless regards return to service without the test as a serious violation, this being respondent's second such finding in three years, the prior instance, at the Wexford garage in the autumn of the first year, having been resolved by warning letter. The license is suspended for 30 days beginning April 1, during which respondent may complete work in progress at four named sites but may accept no new engagements. Reinstatement is conditioned on submission of a revised return to service checklist and on attendance by all six of respondent's mechanics at the Board's procedures seminar. Appeal lies to the full Board within 15 days of this notice.
question: For how many days is the Corvus Lift Services license suspended?

passage: Grant compliance report, Harker Point Historical Society, submitted to the Maritime Heritage Fund, award MH-77, year two of three. The award of 180,000 dollars supports conservation of the pilot schooner Verity, and the Society reports expenditure of 61,000 dollars in the reporting year against a budgeted 70,000 dollars, the variance arising from a delay in white oak delivery described below. Completed this year: replacement of 22 hull planks on the port side, refastening of the garboard strakes with bronze, and recaulking of the deck forward of the mast. The keel scarf repair scheduled for August was deferred when the sawmill contracted to supply white oak lost its kiln to fire in June; a substitute supplier has been secured at a price 8 percent higher, and the Fund's approval of the resulting budget revision is requested as Attachment B. Volunteer hours totaled 3,900, valued under Fund rules at 27 dollars per hour and satisfying the match requirement with a margin of 12,000 dollars. The vessel remained open to visitors on 140 days and received 9,600 of them. Year three work comprises the keel scarf, the rudder trunk, and rigging renewal, and the Society anticipates full expenditure of the remaining 49,000 dollars.
question: How many hull planks were replaced on the port side this year?

passage: Application to the Aviation Division for renewal of heliport license H-92, Mercy Ridge Hospital. passage: Statement of reasons, Planning Inspectorate, appeal 21-0448, land rear of Tullamore Terrace. The appellant sought consent for four dwellings on the former coal yard; the district refused, citing overdevelopment and loss of the mature lime tree at the site's northwest corner. On the first ground the Inspector finds for the appellant: the plot ratio proposed, at 0.42, sits below the 0.5 that the district's own plan contemplates for the street, and the objections on massing rest on a misreading of the section drawings, which show the ridge line 1.2 meters below the terrace opposite. On the second ground the Inspector finds for the district: the lime, assessed in the arboricultural report as having 60 years of safe life remaining, contributes materially to the character of the conservation area, and the appellant's proposed replacement planting of six saplings does not compensate for its loss within any reasonable horizon. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part: consent is granted for a revised scheme of three dwellings submitted at the hearing, which retains the tree within a protective easement of 8 meters radius. Conditions numbering fourteen are attached, including a construction method statement to be approved before any groundworks.
question: How many dwellings does the granted revised scheme contain?

passage: Recall notice filed with the Consumer Products Registry by Brindlewood Toys, notice number RC-2210. The company recalls its wooden stacking carousel, item 4405, sold between March and November of this year, after determining that the topmost spindle bead can detach when the toy is inverted and shaken, presenting a choking hazard to children under three. The defect arises from an adhesive substitution made by a subcontractor in February without notification, contrary to the supply agreement; units manufactured before the substitution, identifiable by a batch stamp of 21 or lower on the underside of the base, are not affected. Approximately 34,000 affected units were sold through 260 retailers at a price of 24 dollars. The company has received six reports of detached beads and no reports of injury. Consumers are offered a full refund or a replacement of the corrected design, distinguishable by an orange stripe on the spindle; returns are accepted by mail with postage prepaid by the company or at any point of sale. The company estimates recall costs at 700,000 dollars and has terminated the subcontract. A progress report is due to the Registry at 60 days and a final report at 180 days.
question: Which batch stamps identify units not affected by the recall?

passage: Application for water withdrawal license renewal, Grigsby Bottling Company, source: the Ansel spring, license file WL-303. The applicant seeks renewal for ten years at the current authorized withdrawal of 90,000 gallons per day, and reports actual average withdrawal of 64,000 gallons per day over the expiring term, with a single day maximum of 88,500 gallons recorded during the plant's anniversary production run in year six. Spring discharge, gauged monthly under the license, averaged 410,000 gallons per day, and the applicant's hydrologist concludes in Appendix 2 that withdrawal at the licensed rate captures 22 percent of mean discharge and leaves the downstream reach above the habitat threshold of 250,000 gallons per day in all months of record save one: September of the drought year, when total discharge itself fell to 240,000 gallons per day and the applicant, under the low flow protocol, reduced withdrawal to 30,000 gallons per day for 19 days. Two objections are on file, both from the Millrace Anglers Association, concerning temperature in the downstream reach; the applicant volunteers continuous temperature logging at the confluence as a renewal condition. The fee of 4,100 dollars accompanies this application. The applicant employs 51 persons at the spring site.
question: What was the applicant's actual average daily withdrawal over the expiring term?

passage: Report of examination, Bureau of Financial Institutions, in the matter of the Weavers Mutual Benefit Association, examination as of December 31. The Association, a burial society founded in 1893 and holding certificate 71, reports 2,140 members and assets of 5.6 million dollars, of which 4.9 million dollars are held in the permitted classes of government paper and insured deposits. The examiners note two matters. First, the Association's investment in the Corriedale office building, carried at 480,000 dollars, exceeds the 5 percent of assets permitted for real property by rule 12; the Association acquired the building by foreclosure in 2016 and has twice been granted extensions to divest. A final extension to June 30 of next year is recommended, after which the excess must be charged against surplus. Second, the actuarial valuation shows the funeral benefit fund at 108 percent of required reserves, down from 114 percent, a decline the examiners attribute to the benefit increase voted at the 2022 assembly without a corresponding dues adjustment; the examiners recommend the board present a dues schedule to the next assembly. Management's responses, accepted as satisfactory, appear at Schedule F. The prior examination found no matters. The next examination falls due in three years.
question: At what value is the Corriedale office building carried?

passage: Notice of intent to construct, filed with the Dam Safety Office by the Larkfield Irrigation District, structure: Coldwater detention basin. The district proposes an earthen embankment 18 feet high and 640 feet long across the Coldwater draw, impounding at design capacity 95 acre feet, placing the structure in the low hazard class provided the downstream trailer court at Beeman's Crossing is counted, as the district contends, outside the inundation zone. The office's preliminary review, attached, disagrees: its modeling of a sunny day failure shows a flow depth of 1.4 feet at the nearest trailer pad, which under the classification rule requires assignment to the significant hazard class and design review accordingly. The district may either accept significant hazard classification, with its requirement of a spillway passing the 500 year event and instrumentation to be read monthly, or revise the design; the office notes that lowering the embankment to 14 feet and capacity to 60 acre feet would, on the same modeling, keep failure flows within the draw. The district's stated purpose is to hold spring runoff for release into the Larkfield canal in July and August, replacing an informal practice of gravel berms rebuilt annually since the 1970s. A response is required within 90 days.
question: What flow depth at the nearest trailer pad did the office's modeling show?

passage: Semiannual progress report under mining reclamation bond MR-4419, Kestrel Slate Quarry, filed by the operator, Bryn and Howell. Reclamation of the exhausted north pit proceeds against the approved plan of 2021. In the reporting period the operator placed 41,000 cubic yards of overburden against a plan of 38,000, completing the backfill of benches 1 through 3; bench 4 remains open as the active haul route and will be the final placement area next year. Topsoil from the stockpile established in 2019 was spread over six acres and seeded with the approved upland mixture; germination inspection in September found cover of 62 percent against the release standard of 70 percent, and the operator will overseed two thin areas totaling 0.8 acres in the spring. The pit lake in the south workings, monitored quarterly, held pH between 7.1 and 7.6, within limits. One deviation is disclosed: a silt fence along the east haul road failed during the August 12 storm, releasing sediment onto 200 feet of the adjoining pasture; the operator removed the deposit, compensated the landowner under a recorded agreement, and doubled the fence in the affected reach. Bond amount remains 640,000 dollars; no reduction is requested this period.
question: How many cubic yards of overburden did the operator place in the reporting period?

passage: Application for certificate of public convenience, filed by Solverne Ambulance Service with the Emergency Services Commission, docket ES-1204. The applicant seeks designation as second provider for the Grand Fork response zone, where the incumbent, Pelham Rescue, has held sole designation since 1998. The applicant proposes to station one advanced life support unit at the Solverne fire hall around the clock and a second unit at the Grand Fork substation from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m., staffed by a roster of 19 personnel of whom eleven hold paramedic certification. In support, the applicant cites the zone's response statistics for the past two years: average response of 14.8 minutes against the state benchmark of 12 minutes, with the far orchard district averaging 21 minutes. The incumbent's opposition, filed under the same docket, attributes the averages to the zone's geography, notes its own addition of a third crew in the spring, and argues that dividing a call volume of 2,300 annual responses will degrade the proficiency of both providers. The commission's hearing examiner has ordered a joint workshop on dispatch protocols before the evidentiary hearing, set for October 2, and has invited the county's three fire companies to intervene by September 1.
question: What was the zone's average response time over the past two years?
